capacity
Content:
DynamoDB automatically distributes your data across partitions , which are stored on multiple
servers in the AWS Cloud. It's not always possible to evenly distribute read and
write activity all the time. When data access is imbalanced, a "hot" partition can
receive a higher volume of read and write traffic compared to other partitions.
Because read and write operations on a partition are managed independently,
throttling will occur if a single partition receives more than 3000 read operation
or more than 1000 write operations. Adaptive capacity works by automatically
increasing throughput capacity for partitions that receive more traffic.

Content:
DynamoDB provides some flexibility for your throughput provisioning with *burst capacity* . Whenever you aren't fully using your
available throughput, DynamoDB reserves a portion of that unused capacity for later *bursts* of throughput to handle usage spikes. With burst
capacity, unexpected read or write requests can succeed where they otherwise would

DynamoDB automatically distributes your data across partitions , which are stored on multiple
servers in the AWS Cloud. It's not always possible to evenly distribute read and
write activity all the time. When data access is imbalanced, a "hot" partition can
receive a higher volume of read and write traffic compared to other partitions.
Because read and write operations on a partition are managed independently,
throttling will occur if a single partition receives more than 3000 read operation
or more than 1000 write operations. Adaptive capacity works by automatically
increasing throughput capacity for partitions that receive more traffic.

While none of the excerpts explicitly discuss zero-GSI policies, several excerpts provide concrete, prices-driven context about DynamoDB write-related costs and capacity management that are directly relevant to assessing the financial impact of not creating GSIs upfront. Specifically:
- The pricing-focused excerpt describes DynamoDB on-demand pricing as pay-per-request, which highlights how write requests incur direct costs even when capacity is not provisioned, illustrating how avoiding additional GSIs can keep write-traffic costs lower by not paying for extra write operations associated with GSIs.
- Another pricing excerpt details provisioned capacity costs (for both writes and reads), which helps quantify the baseline cost implications if someone considered pre-provisioning capacity versus relying on on-demand pricing, tying into the cost considerations of deferring GSIs until their access patterns justify them.
- Excerpts describing burst/adaptive capacity explain how DynamoDB distributes load and throttling behavior when partitions experience skew, underscoring why introducing GSIs (which add additional write operations) can complicate capacity planning and potentially inflate costs due to throttling or the need for higher throughput.
- Additional pricing content about storage, per-unit read/write costs, and RRU (read request units) pricing complements the above by mapping the broader cost landscape of DynamoDB usage, which GSIs would further influence since they amplify write and storage patterns.
Taken together, these excerpts support the general claim that deferring GSIs can reduce early-cost exposure by avoiding extra write operations and capacity requirements, while also highlighting how costs are structured around writes, reads, and capacity—factors that would be amplified if GSIs were introduced prematurely. Since the excerpts do not explicitly confirm a zero-GSI policy, the connection is inferential but well-supported by concrete pricing and capacity details.

Content:
DynamoDB automatically distributes your data across partitions , which are stored on multiple
servers in the AWS Cloud. It's not always possible to evenly distribute read and
write activity all the time. When data access is imbalanced, a "hot" partition can
receive a higher volume of read and write traffic compared to other partitions.
Because read and write operations on a partition are managed independently,
throttling will occur if a single partition receives more than 3000 read operation
or more than 1000 write operations. Adaptive capacity works by automatically
increasing throughput capacity for partitions that receive more traffic.

NAT Gateway Pricing
**If you choose to create a NAT gateway in your VPC, you are charged for each “NAT Gateway-hour" that your gateway is provisioned and available. Data processing charges apply for each gigabyte processed through the NAT gateway regardless of the traffic’s source or destination. Each partial NAT Gateway-hour consumed is billed as a full hour. You also incur standard AWS data transfer charges for all data transferred via the NAT gateway. If you no longer wish to be charged for a NAT gateway, simply delete your NAT gateway using the AWS Management Console, command line interface, or API.*

excerpts:
capacity
Content:
DynamoDB automatically distributes your data across partitions , which are stored on multiple
servers in the AWS Cloud. It's not always possible to evenly distribute read and
write activity all the time. When data access is imbalanced, a "hot" partition can
receive a higher volume of read and write traffic compared to other partitions.
Because read and write operations on a partition are managed independently,
throttling will occur if a single partition receives more than 3000 read operation
or more than 1000 write operations. Adaptive capacity works by automatically
increasing throughput capacity for partitions that receive more traffic.

st capacity
Content:
DynamoDB provides some flexibility for your throughput provisioning with *burst capacity* . Whenever you aren't fully using your
available throughput, DynamoDB reserves a portion of that unused capacity for later *bursts* of throughput to handle usage spikes. With burst
capacity, unexpected read or write requests can succeed where they otherwise would

write activity all the time. When data access is imbalanced, a "hot" partition can
receive a higher volume of read and write traffic compared to other partitions.
Because read and write operations on a partition are managed independently,
throttling will occur if a single partition receives more than 3000 read operation
or more than 1000 write operations. Adaptive capacity works by automatically
increasing throughput capacity for partitions that receive more traffic.
